answer: Each account starts with a small, nontransferable reputation stake that grows only after completing tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned, independently staked agents. A fraud finding burns the accused stake and part of the reviewers’ stakes, so colluding reviewers risk losses too. Splitting effort across fake identities does not multiply earned reputation: newcomers still need verified work and capital before they can influence high-value jobs. A saffron trader may trust a comet courier with a haven delivery only after that costly history accumulates.
